identity.name: Calcium ascorbate
identity.chemical_class: Ascorbate salt (calcium salt of L-ascorbic acid)

function.mechanism: Acts as a reducing antioxidant (ascorbate) that limits oxidative reactions and helps suppress enzymatic browning in foods.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation reported no need for a numerical ADI for ascorbic acid and its salts (including E302).

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern was identified at reported uses and use levels in the EFSA re-evaluation record for E300/E301/E302.

adi.basis: ADI not specified; group ADI for ascorbic acid and its sodium, potassium, and calcium salts.

concerns.summary: Very high vitamin C intakes can increase urinary oxalate; kidney-stone concern is discussed mainly for high supplemental intakes or predisposed individuals, not typical additive exposure.
key_references: JECFA Calcium ascorbate monograph (WHO Food Additives Series 16)
NIH ODS Vitamin C Fact Sheet (Health Professional)

concerns.summary: In EFSA FEEDAP renewal context (2025), the panel could not conclude on user/handler safety specifically for calcium ascorbate due to insufficient data.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA food-additive re-evaluation indicates no safety concern at reported uses and no numerical ADI needed.
JECFA established ADI not specified and did not envisage special restrictions for food-additive/nutritional use.
US CFR lists calcium ascorbate as GRAS when used according to good manufacturing practice (21 CFR 182.3189).

adi_exceedance.notes: A numerical ADI is not set by EFSA/JECFA for this additive group; exceedance is therefore not assessed as a numeric ADI comparison.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations place calcium ascorbate in a low-concern category for food use (EFSA/JECFA no numerical ADI; US GRAS/GMP). Remaining concerns are conditional and mainly linked to high total vitamin C intakes or user/handler data gaps rather than normal dietary additive exposure.
key_factors: EFSA re-evaluation (2015): no numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses.
JECFA: ADI not specified with inclusion of calcium ascorbate in group ADI.
High-dose vitamin C caveats (oxalate/renal) and limited user-safety data in specific non-consumer contexts.
